notes.title: "Update++"
notes.content:
Well, look who’s back! It’s hard to believe it’s been five years since Hero’s Spirit first hit the scene, right?

[i]Hero’s Spirit[/i] has always been a true passion project—a labor of love. But, oh boy, what a journey it’s been. There were ups and downs, some things that didn’t quite land, and a whole lot of engine rewrites (seriously, I lost count). We’ve poured countless hours into the game, fine-tuning every little detail. And honestly, if things had gone any differently, Hero’s Spirit wouldn’t be [i]this [/i]Hero’s Spirit. But hey, we’ve learned a ton—about user experience, accessibility, community, and managing a project this big. Sometimes, we weren’t putting our best foot forward (though we thought we were!), but the great thing is, we’re always improving. And we’re nowhere near done yet.

Now, let’s talk about what’s new. The last couple of years may have been quiet here on Steam, but behind the scenes? [i]Pure chaos[/i]. Even more engine rewrites, and the art team has been hard at work. And before we knew it… yeah, years had flown by. The “[i]future[/i]” we were building wasn’t quite ready to deliver, but we couldn’t just leave you all hanging forever. So, we dug around the repos, grabbed the best of what we’d worked on, and put together a fresh branch to move forward with. (By the way, this isn’t the “[i]DX[/i]” upgrade people have been talking about—we’re still cooking something up, but we didn’t want to leave you waiting around.)

And now, drumroll, please... here comes [b]Update++[/b]! This update is a [i]game-changer[/i] (lol), with major quality of life improvements across the board. You’ll see a new “memory” system for areas outside your line of sight. There are new shaders to pick from in Settings. The story has been expanded, and the rabbit hole now has a proper, satisfying end. There are two brand-new unlockable game modes—one’s an auto-runner, and the other’s a hardcore challenge mode for those ready for an even greater difficulty. Oh, and there are [i]tons [/i]of small quality-of-life improvements throughout the whole experience. And certainly not least of all, a whole bunch of shiny new achievements to unlock!

Alright, enough talk. Let’s dive into the [b]CHANGELOG[/b]!

[list]
[*] Fixed several instances of incorrect tile colorations during special events
[*] New very-late-game event is available in the Tundra map, and leads to further content
[*] Improved snake-type enemy behaviors
[*] Adds a new unlockable auto-runner mode (unlocked the same way as the BFF achievement)
[*] BFF achievement is no longer earned for dead/undead pets
[*] Can no longer leave mounts in boss fights (or in some cases, take them in at all)
[*] The main game has multiple new endings
[*] North and South Mundeman are now combined into a single "Mundeman" map during a certain game mode
[*] Flower tiles are now colorful and much easier to identify
[*] Completion display is no longer garbled if negative
[*] New "mode selection" submenu is available when starting the game once more than one mode has been unlocked
[*] Rom path is now specified via 'rom.txt' in the game's directory
[*] Tons of object cleanup on the backend of things
[*] Base resolution has changed - the game is now 16:9 by default, and is considerably more flexible in letter/pillar-boxing
[*] The game now has basic support for multiple monitors. You should be able to fullscreen the game (F11, or Alt+Enter) to any monitor
[*] Added "Heroic Hardcore" mode. This is automatically unlocked at the game's final ending, or you can type "HEROIC" on the new mode select submenu (once unlocked) to unlock it at any time
[*] The Eye of the Collector is now context-aware and will not point to items that are conceptually in a different region
[*] The Eye of the Collector now seems to point to doors that can be opened, if it's got nothing better to do
[*] Retro/CRT shader now defaults to off. There is also a new Smooth shader that can be used instead
[*] There may be yet another secret game mode (or two)
[*] There is now a rain effect that will be present in a couple maps
[*] Fixed map load time issues in some circumstances, should be more consistent
[*] Removed V-Sync- the underlying library has a troublesome implementation that behaves inconsistently. We'll just have to do the best we can without it, and revisit this in the future
[*] Added tameable horses
[*] Reworked the convergence maps and the relevant boss fight
[*] Fixed several bugs related to Cat kills
[*] Fixed a flaw with step counts in a certain circumstance
[*] Reworked completion % calculation to be slightly less arcane and slightly more intuitive
[*] Reworked game mode progression; as a general rule, progression now revolves primarily around just reaching the appropriate/relevant ending
[*] The numbers matter
[*] Probably fixed "item skipping" with some fancy shoes
[*] Fixed numerous texture leaks (and a texture corruption bug), should reduce VRAM footprint
[*] Color swords/shields are now progressive, and you will always find whichever is next in that slot's progression
[*] Rumor has it that a new tier of Color swords/shields is now legitimately obtainable
[*] Cosmetics now properly support lava and death colorations
[*] New unlockable cosmetic options have been added, one of which has special effects
[*] Volume settings have been reimplemented in a more balanced way- should be easier to configure and more in line with other applications
[*] Visual cues have been added to some puzzles, like switches or breakable walls
[*] "Windroutes" have been smoothed and shortened in most cases
[*] Countless tile adjustments, polish, and fixes
[*] The shrine can be re-sealed after the relevant event has ended
[*] The bloodmoon event now has a playlist of new music instead of a single short track
[*] Tons of new music (the soundtrack doubled with this update)
[*] 35 new achievements are now available to earn (bringing the total to 50), spanning the entire game
[/list]

notes.title: Quality of Life Update
notes.content:
A quality of life update has been pushed to Steam. Lots of fixes here, folks. (Though let's be realistic, we probably broke something as well and are standing by for reports.)

[b]This is not [i]New Gen+[/i][/b], please read the previous announcement, [i]The Future of Hero's Spirit[/i], for more information on that.

• updated backend to .NET 6.0 and updated all dependencies
• possible (needs verification!) fix for Intel HD3000 series GPUs
• improved rendering performance
• added vsync to settings
• fixed framerate when vsync is off
• fixed tool-assist mode's 100% speed being too slow
• fixed tool-assist mode's MAX speed capping at refresh rate
• fixed bad visual stuttering on windows 11
• fixed wrong framerate on windows 11
• new castle grounds (normal/+) music, day & night
• added a second hidden entrance to the dragon's lair (resolves a certain softlock)
• certain misplaced friends can be recovered at sanctuary
• took the machine guns away from cats
• cats now prefer to be 'near' the player rather than 'touching' the player.
• cats no longer follow the player if the player is mounted
• bunnies no longer snack on their largest friends
• cats no longer snack on their largest friends
• bunnies follow the player through noneuclidean areas without getting weird about it
• off-border color while -not- using the retro shader will now match the HUD background
• Luddershore++ has a new color scheme and tunes
• frank can now frank even when the franking would otherwise have been defranked
• fixed a bad stripe of location text in the mountains in the castle grounds
• you are now ready for this place (if you are ready for it)
• cats now enjoy the occasional crunchy snack
• portals in the swamp are now properly labeled
• the forbidden shore can be accessed
• wait, they _do_ come in red??
• flashing items on the HUD are a bit smoother
• the post-credits scene now displays kill count
• the 'hole' NPC is less incorrect
• added "Open Data Folder" to Settings menu

notes.title: The Collector's Update is Live!
notes.content:
- Added: A completely new HUD, including new items and location names.
- Added: A crystal has been unearthed, one that resembles the save crystals scattered across the world.
- Added: A mysterious artifact known as the Broom has been discovered. Spiders beware!
- Added: A new shop operated by an unknown stranger has appeared.
- Added: A new vegetable, the Carrot, has been imported from overseas.
- Added: A strange mirror with unusual depth has been discovered.
- Added: Beginning a new game+ will add a "Start Game+" option to the pre-game menu.
- Added: Five new achievements.
- Added: Multiple new music tracks.
- Added: Multiple new maps.
- Added: Multiple new map colorations.
- Added: NPCs are much more talkative, and their dialogue changes throughout the game.
- Added: Strange new coins are scattered around the world.
- Added: The compass now points towards the nearest save point, if one exists on the current map.
- Added: The Eye of the Collector has been discovered.
- Added: The line of sight mechanic now has alternative textures in options to reduce eye-strain reported by some players.
- Added: The player can make new friends who will follow them on their journey.
- Added: The player now leaves a trail of crumbs when they pass through hidden paths.
- Added: Unlockable cosmetic options.
- Fixed: A mysterious key has been restrained from ending the world by closing your game unnecessarily.
- Fixed: Convinces secret tiles that they should keep their palettes up to date.
- Fixed: Gave the treasure counter in the castle grounds a good talking to, made sure it never lies to the player.
- Fixed: Sat the main character down and explained that facing south every time they enter a new map is unnecessary.
- Fixed: The bunny has been provided a booster shot to immunize it against certain environmental hazards.
- Fixed: The exit menu now has a minor delay when closed, reducing unwanted button input.
- Fixed: The portals in Sanctuary are better at pretending to be brick walls when inactive.
- Fixed: The witch is now a good sport and kicks you out of unwinnable fights if you have a bad equipment combination.
- Fixed: The witch can no longer freeze time under specific unusual circumstances.
- Fixed: There were no misplaced map tiles to fix. Reports to the contrary certainly weren't addressed.

And all the stuff in between the lines here. We really hope you enjoy this update :heart:

notes.title: Coming Very Soon: The Collector's Update
notes.content:
It's come to our attention that a certain one of our players has very nearly completed the dive, all the way to the bottom of the game. In a desperate attempt to slow them down, we've contrived a small, simple update that just adds a couple new maps, a handful of new equipment, a sprinkling of quality of life features, some unlockable cosmetic options, a new collectable item type, a couple new mechanics, a new music track, a redesign of the HUD, a new shop, fast travel enhancements, escalates your relationship with a certain NPC, addresses some complaints, and [strike]smells vaguely like chicken but only on Thursdays[/strike]. (edit: so, it turns out the chicken thing wasn't true. sorry folks, I was misinformed.)

Front and center, the star of the show, is a new piece of equipment: [i]The Eye of the Collector[/i]. This item will help you, sort of, as you attempt to track down all those pesky items scattered about. So grab that and- what's that? Where is it? We can't just tell you that. The world's only so big, right? Go find it! Hint, it's not just laying out in the open.

[b]So when does this go live? Just as soon as we can finish it! (Original plan was this weekend, but we decided to let it bake just a little bit longer because the quality will be that much better.) Trust me, we're working fast to make this happen ASAP, and are already making good time.[/b]

notes.title: View Distance Update
notes.content:
[h2][b]Hero's Spirit: View Distance Update[/b][/h2]

Hello everyone! An update for Hero's Spirit has just gone live.  With it comes a new parameter in the Settings menu, called [i]View Distance[/i].

[img]https://i.imgur.com/xhsceO1.png[/img]

Defaults to [i]Original[/i] which is the game as you currently know it; but you can change it to [i]Enhanced[/i] to increase visibility in certain situations, such as thick forests. This setting will make collection efforts easier, the choice of whether to use this new feature is up to you.

Comparisons:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/y70Yym4.png[/img]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/XRulfFd.png[/img]

There is now a slight buff to the view distance in the direction the hero is facing. Previously, visibility was omni-directional regardless of facing direction, and still is, but you will see a bit more clearly in the facing direction while in [i]Enhanced[/i] mode.  There are more nuanced changes as well in [i]Enhanced[/i] view distance which reduce some of the noise and flickering as you wander through open spaces.  

These changes were very carefully crafted to eliminate zero-warning combat situations and slightly reduce screen flicker, while still being close to the original design. Forests and spiderwebs are still dangerous, but you will have the opportunity to react if moving cautiously.

Thank you for playing our game, and we hope you continue to enjoy it!

Cheers!
~ TBI
